rows.grounds: epithet or name referring to the sacred basil plant; nominative form in a series of divine names
compound epithet: tulasī (holy basil) + varyā (excellent, best); denotes preeminence associated with tulasī
compound epithet: tulā (balance, scale) + jā (born); denotes origin or arising from balance
compound epithet: tulajā (balance-born) + īśvarī (sovereign lady, mistress); denotes rulership over or identity as the balance-born

items.question: Which sacred and balance-born sovereign identities are ascribed to the goddess in these epithets?
premises: The epithet tulasī identifies the goddess with the sacred basil.
The epithet tulasīvaryā attributes excellence connected to the sacred basil.
The epithets tulajā and tulajeśvarī attribute a balance-born origin and sovereign ladyship.
items.inference: The goddess is praised through a sequence of names linking her to the sacred basil and to sovereign identity arising from balance.
uncertainties: Whether tulā in tulajā and tulajeśvarī refers specifically to the zodiacal sign Libra, a weighing scale, or balance as an abstract principle is not determined by the verse alone.
items.plain_english: She is Tulasī, the excellent Tulasī, the one born of balance, and the sovereign lady of those born of balance.
